source: Zelikman et al. (2022) STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
finding: Loop: sample rationales, keep those whose final answer is correct, fine-tune, repeat. Early form of outcome-reward-only reasoning training (expert iteration).
numbers: GPT-J 6B. CommonsenseQA: STaR with rationalization 72.5% vs direct fine-tuned GPT-3 (30x larger) 73.0%; STaR without rationalization 68.8%.
limits: Rationalization (hint with the correct answer) is a non-RL add-on; multiple-choice makes lucky-correct rationales likely.
agent_relevance: Shows that a correct final answer is a usable filter for reasoning traces. We only prompt, but this is the root of the verifiable-reward idea.

source: Zelikman et al. (2022) STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
finding: On GSM8K the same loop gives gains while using a fraction of the training data.
numbers: GSM8K test: few-shot CoT 3.1%, direct fine-tune 5.8%, STaR no rationalization 10.1% (25.0% of train data used), with rationalization 10.7% (28.7%).
limits: Low absolute numbers with a 6B model from 2022; wrong-reasoning-right-answer traces are kept.
agent_relevance: Outcome checks admit flawed reasoning; our scaffold should check steps, not only the answer.

source: Shao et al. (2024) DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models (introduces GRPO)
finding: GRPO drops the PPO critic: for each question sample a group of outputs and use the group reward mean and spread as the baseline. Cuts memory and compute.
numbers: DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B to RL: GSM8K 82.9% to 88.2%, MATH 46.8% to 51.7%, CMATH 84.6% to 88.8%; instruction-tuning data only.
limits: 7B model; reward is a learned reward model in this paper, not purely rule-based.
agent_relevance: Group-relative scoring is the same idea as sampling several candidates and ranking them; it is the core of RLVR training.

source: Shao et al. (2024) DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models (introduces GRPO)
finding: Early finding that RL sharpens rather than widens: Maj@K improves but Pass@K does not.
numbers: Figure 7 (GSM8K, MATH, temperature 0.7): RL raises Maj@K; Pass@K of RL model about equal to instruct model.
limits: One 7B model and two benchmarks; read from figure and text.
agent_relevance: Anticipates the later boundary debate. Voting over samples at inference captures much of the gain RL gives.
quote: RL enhances Maj@K's performance but not Pass@K

source: Shao et al. (2024) DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models (introduces GRPO)
finding: Unified view: SFT, rejection-sampling fine-tuning, DPO, PPO and GRPO are variants of one gradient with different data source, reward and coefficient. Online sampling beats offline.
numbers: Paper compares online vs offline RFT and iterative RL; iterative RL gives the biggest gain at the first iteration.
limits: 7B experiments only.
agent_relevance: Online use of the model's own samples with a checker is the strong variant; our propose-and-check loop mirrors it at test time.

source: Lambert et al. (2024) Tulu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training
finding: Names RLVR: a constant reward if the completion is verifiably correct, else zero, applied to math and precise instruction following; used as last step after SFT and DPO.
numbers: Tulu 3 405B RLVR on MATH only: even 25 RLVR steps raised MATH by over 5 points and it kept rising. Initialising the value function from a general reward model gave best GSM8K.
limits: Gains are in targeted domains; more KL budget did not always raise reward. PPO, not GRPO.
agent_relevance: Origin of the term. Verifiable checks (math, instruction constraints) are the cheap signal; our scaffold can use the same checks at run time.
quote: RLVR ... obtains a constant reward value if a completion is successful.

source: Lambert et al. (2024) Tulu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training
finding: RLVR gains are domain-specific; IFEval over-optimisation was observed and an out-of-distribution IFEval-OOD set was built to detect it.
numbers: Appendix B.4 and Section 7.3.1; RLVR on GSM8K, MATH and IFEval each improved its own test set.
limits: Per-model table values vary by size and were not all extracted.
agent_relevance: A verifier-trained skill can be narrow. Test on shifted constraints.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
finding: R1-Zero: pure RL (GRPO) on the base model with only two rewards, accuracy (rule-checkable answers, code tests) and format (think/answer tags), equal weight. No neural reward model for reasoning tasks.
numbers: AIME 2024 pass@1 rose from 15.6% to 77.9% during RL; with majority vote 86.7%.
limits: Base model is DeepSeek-V3-Base (large). Only rule-checkable problems.
agent_relevance: The recipe behind the reasoning-model wave; the behaviours it produces are what our scaffold tries to elicit by prompting.
quote: we abstain from applying neural reward models--whether outcome-based or process-based--to reasoning tasks

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
finding: Reported emergent aha moment: response length grows and the model starts to reflect and re-check ('Wait, wait').
numbers: Table 2 shows one intermediate R1-Zero trace; length grows steadily over RL steps (Figure 1).
limits: One anecdote; Dr. GRPO finds such behaviour already in base models.
agent_relevance: Reflection and re-check are our verify operators; they appear without being taught.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
finding: R1-Zero had poor readability and language mixing, so R1 adds cold-start SFT data, a language-consistency reward, rejection-sampling SFT and a second RL stage with helpfulness (66,000 pairs) and safety (106,000) reward models.
numbers: R1 vs OpenAI o1-1217 (paper table): AIME 2024 79.8 vs 79.2, MATH-500 97.3 vs 96.4, GPQA Diamond 71.5 vs 75.7.
limits: Numbers are the paper's own evaluation, averaged over many samples; column assignment read from text layout.
agent_relevance: Pure verifiable RL is not enough for a usable assistant; style and safety need other signals.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
finding: Authors state limits: reliable rule-based rewards exist only for verifiable tasks; scaling pure RL for tasks without a reliable reward is open; language mixing outside Chinese and English.
numbers: Limitations section; no new measurement.
limits: Statements, not measurements.
agent_relevance: Our agent must supply its own checks (tests, calculators, re-derivation) where no verifier exists.

source: Kimi Team (2025) Kimi k1.5: Scaling Reinforcement Learning with LLMs
finding: Independent long-context RL result without Monte Carlo tree search, value functions or process reward models; uses partial rollouts to make long chains affordable and long2short methods to shorten them.
numbers: Long-CoT model: AIME 77.5, MATH-500 96.2, Codeforces 94th percentile, MathVista 74.9 (paper says matches o1).
limits: Closed model; data mix only partly described.
agent_relevance: Simple outcome rewards plus long context suffice; long2short shows shorter reasoning can be distilled back.

source: Yu et al. (2025) DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
finding: Reproduction gap: naive GRPO on Qwen2.5-32B reached only 30 on AIME 2024 vs 47 reported for DeepSeek R1-Zero-style RL. They found entropy collapse, reward noise and instability.
numbers: Naive GRPO 30; DAPO 50 on AIME 2024 with Qwen2.5-32B.
limits: They say critical details were missing from the R1 paper.
agent_relevance: The headline recipe was not reproducible as published; treat reported RL gains with care.
quote: naive GRPO baseline suffers from several key issues such as entropy collapse, reward noise, and training instability

source: Yu et al. (2025) DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
finding: Four fixes: Clip-Higher (decoupled clip range keeps entropy), Dynamic Sampling (drop prompts whose group is all-correct or all-wrong), token-level policy-gradient loss, overlong reward shaping.
numbers: Ablation figures show AIME avg@32 rising with each piece; entropy collapses without Clip-Higher.
limits: Ablation on one model and one dataset.
agent_relevance: RLVR needs sample diversity; same lesson for our candidate generation.

source: Liu et al. (2025) Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective (Dr. GRPO)
finding: GRPO has a length and std-normalisation bias that favours long wrong answers; Dr. GRPO removes both and gives better token efficiency.
numbers: Minimalist recipe on Qwen2.5-Math-7B with MATH level 3-5 questions: 43.3% on AIME 2024, 27 hours on 8 A100 GPUs.
limits: Small, math-pretrained base model.
agent_relevance: Part of apparent longer thinking is an optimiser artefact; do not equate length with quality.

source: Liu et al. (2025) Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective (Dr. GRPO)
finding: Base models already have the skills: nearly all base models, including DeepSeek-V3-Base, show the aha moment; Qwen2.5 bases improve about 60% immediately when no template is used.
numbers: Section 2.2: about 60% immediate improvement without template; template mismatch can destroy ability before RL repairs it.
limits: Contamination reading is a hypothesis.
agent_relevance: Prompt format matters hugely; test scaffold prompts against format effects.

source: Yue et al. (2025) Does RL Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
finding: With pass@k at large k, RLVR models win at small k but base models catch up and surpass at large k across math, code and visual benchmarks and model families. RLVR narrows the boundary.
numbers: Base models consistently surpass RLVR models as k grows; k=256 used as proxy for base ceiling; six RLVR algorithms perform similarly and stay far from optimal.
limits: Mostly Qwen and Llama up to 32B; contested by ProRL.
agent_relevance: If RL mostly sharpens sampling, sample-many-and-verify at inference reaches the same place without training.
quote: base models achieve higher pass@k score when k is large

source: Yue et al. (2025) Does RL Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
finding: Coverage and perplexity analysis: RLVR reasoning paths already lie in the base model's sampling distribution. Distillation adds new patterns and expands the boundary.
numbers: Distilled model exceeds base boundary in their figure; RLVR models do not.
limits: Cannot rule out longer or more diverse training.
agent_relevance: Strong-teacher demonstrations add capability where self-RL does not.

source: Shao et al. (2025) Spurious Rewards: Rethinking Training Signals in RLVR
finding: Random, format-only and incorrect-label rewards raise MATH-500 for Qwen2.5-Math models almost as much as ground truth.
numbers: Qwen2.5-Math-7B MATH-500 gain: ground truth +29.1 points, random +21.4; Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B 36.2% to 60.4% in one table row (+24.2).
limits: Does not transfer: Qwen2.5, OLMo2 and Llama3 show minimal gain or loss under spurious rewards.
agent_relevance: Many RLVR gains on Qwen measure amplification of pretraining habits, not learning from the verifier. Do not trust Qwen-only evidence.
quote: RLVR can elicit strong mathematical reasoning in certain language models even with spurious rewards

source: Shao et al. (2025) Spurious Rewards: Rethinking Training Signals in RLVR
finding: Mechanism: GRPO clipping bias amplifies high-prior behaviours. For Qwen2.5-Math-7B that is code reasoning (Python-style reasoning with no execution).
numbers: Code reasoning in 65.0% of MATH-500 answers rises to over 90% with spurious rewards; those answers are more accurate.
limits: Shown for Qwen only; Llama and OLMo lack the amplifiable behaviour.
agent_relevance: A strategy already likely in the model is what gets boosted; we can prompt such strategies directly.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning in LLMs with One Training Example
finding: One training example gives large RLVR gains on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B; part of it is format correction.
numbers: MATH500 36.0% to 73.6% with 1 example (8.6 points beyond format correction); six-benchmark average 17.6% to 35.7% (7.0 non-format); equals the 1.2k DeepScaleR subset (73.6%, 35.9%); 2 examples 74.8% and 36.6%.
limits: Qwen-heavy; effect also on Llama3.2-3B-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B.
agent_relevance: RLVR mostly elicits an existing skill and output format; prompt format may do the same.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning in LLMs with One Training Example
finding: Post-saturation generalisation: test accuracy keeps rising after training accuracy saturates; effect comes from policy-gradient loss, not grokking; entropy loss for exploration matters; self-reflection frequency rises.
numbers: Seen with GRPO and PPO and several example choices; cross-category generalisation reported.
limits: Mechanism claims rest on ablations on a few models.
agent_relevance: Rising self-reflection supports keeping a reflection state in the schema.

source: Liu et al. (2025) ProRL: Prolonged Reinforcement Learning Expands Reasoning Boundaries in LLMs
finding: Counter to Yue et al.: with KL control, reference-policy resets and 136K diverse verifiable problems, prolonged RL widens the boundary, including tasks where the base model fails at every k.
numbers: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B: average pass@1 +14.7% math, +13.9% code, +54.8% logic puzzles, +25.1% STEM, +18.1% instruction following; beats domain-specialised baselines by +4.6% math and +6.5% code.
limits: Starts from a distilled 1.5B model; boundary gains track base-model competence on the task and training length; heavy compute.
agent_relevance: Boundary debate is open: new ability needs long, diverse training. For our no-training agent, assume the base boundary.

source: Shao et al. (2025) Spurious Rewards: Rethinking Training Signals in RLVR
finding: Non-Qwen models do not benefit from spurious rewards: format or incorrect rewards give flat or negative results on OLMo2-7B and Llama3.1-8B-Instruct; OLMo2-7B-SFT gains only on some signals.
numbers: OLMo2-7B-SFT gains about +8.9 and +5.5 on some reward types (appendix text); base OLMo2 stays flat under spurious rewards, gains mainly with ground truth.
limits: Exact per-model table not re-extracted.
agent_relevance: Findings from one model family may not generalise; validate on several.
quote: effect depends critically on the base model

source: Liu et al. (2025) Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective (Dr. GRPO)
finding: Math pretraining raises the RL ceiling: Llama-3.2-3B with math pretraining reaches a higher RL result than without.
numbers: Section 3.4 takeaway: math pretraining on Llama-3.2-3B improves its RL ceiling.
limits: Numbers not extracted here.
agent_relevance: RL gains are bounded by what pretraining put in; supports relying on the base model's skills.
